The Left Hand of God by Paul Hoffman - Three book series that details medieval warfare. The series follows a young man who is the proclaimed messiah of the redeemers cult. He is expected to bring about the end of the world by killing everyone (not kidding). Lots of historical parallels with a boots on the ground view of death and destruction.

The Book of the New Sun - Gene Wolfe. Follows a torturer who refuses to kill a young woman after he is cast out from the torturers. He is trained to execute and torture prisoners. Follow along in traditional fantasy fashion on a journey through the world. Very well written.

And my favorite but it is a blend of sci-fi and fantasy.
The Hyperion Cantos- Dan Simmons. The four book series explores humanistic themes and takes a pretty deep look into both religion and technology. The first book is a sci-fi inspired take on The Canterbury Tales with others looking into the old testament, huck finn, and buddhism. That being said it's not religion in sci-fi clothing. Simmons' explores these stories on the archetypal level. Dan Simmons' books are extraordinarily well written and thought provoking in general. This series is definitely worth reading. It's the best fantasy series I've ever read.
